import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between petal dimensions
# and how they differentiate the species. Petal dimensions usually show
# a clearer separation between Iris species than sepal dimensions.
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species',
    s=100,  # Increase point size for better visibility
    palette='viridis', # Choose a distinct color palette
    alpha=0.8
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Iris Petal Length vs. Petal Width by Species', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)

# Add a legend to identify species
plt.legend(title='Species', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
